description: GAP-5 (bean qou-hinv, epic qou-xu6t): the cusp-shape-drift objection to the merged #4401 lattice sign result. LITERATURE NEGATIVE: Purcell's 'Cusp shapes under cone deformation' (library/arxiv-math-0410233v4/0410233v4.pdf) Theorem 1.2 requires a cone deformation along a singular locus Σ DISJOINT from the cusp T, cone angles 0→2π, with T remaining a cusp throughout — not the QOU setup, where the substrate deformation is the Neumann–Zagier deformation of the 4₁ cusp ITSELF (u = 2 ln q₀ ≠ 0). Purcell's bounds therefore do NOT transfer and cannot close the objection; recorded as an applicability negative rather than a citation of convenience. WHAT REPLACES IT: the objection is real and self-directed (the lattice uses ω at the COMPLETE structure while evaluation sits at u ≠ 0), so the decidable question is how much drift the conclusions tolerate. Generalising to an arbitrary modulus, G_τ(m,ℓ) = (m+ℓτ₁)² − ℓ²τ₂² (reduces exactly to (2m+ℓ)²−3ℓ² at τ = e^{iπ/3}): the MERIDIAN (1,0) gives G_τ = 1 for every modulus, so the muon-side boost sign is exactly immune to drift; the LONGITUDE (0,1) flips only when arg τ crosses π/4 from π/3, a worst-case drift of ~19.5% of |ω| against a plausible O(u) = O(ln q₀) ≈ 10.4% drift scale — a safety margin of ~1.9×. A tolerance bound, NOT a rigidity proof: dω/du is not computed here and remains the open piece. No Δ_λ, no magnitude, nothing wired.

drift_robustness.purcell_applicability: Theorem 1.2 needs singular locus DISJOINT from the cusp, cone angle 0→2π; QOU deforms the cusp itself ⇒ does not apply
drift_robustness.meridian_immunity: G_τ(1,0) = 1 for every modulus τ — boost side exactly drift-immune
drift_robustness.open_piece: dω/du (deformed cusp shape from the A-polynomial) not computed
drift_robustness.verdict: Purcell does not apply (honest applicability negative); the sign result tolerates ~19.5% modulus drift vs a ~10.4% plausible scale (~1.9× margin), and the meridian side is exactly immune — a bound, not a rigidity proof
